Vacuous

VAK-yoo-uhs · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Vacuous is showing a lack of thought, intelligence, or serious content.

The talk show host's vacuous chatter filled the airtime without ever saying anything memorable.

Worked Example

The motivational poster's vacuous slogan -- 'Dream Big, Achieve More' -- offered no actual advice for anyone struggling to reach their goals.

The words sound inspiring but contain no real substance or thought, which is exactly what makes a phrase vacuous.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — vacu- (vacuus)

root — vacu- (vacuus): empty (also seen in vacant and vacuum) (Latin vacuus)

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Vacuous comes from Latin vacuus, 'empty' -- the same root behind vacant and vacuum. Something vacuous is full of emptiness: no real thought, substance, or intelligence behind it.

Use the root in a new word: vacant

Use the root in a new word: vacant: The old theater had sat vacant for a decade before the city finally sold the building.
